tool: Neo4j (AuraDB, GraphRAG, Context Engine, Aura Agent, Virtual Graph)
category: Graph database plus AI knowledge layer (GraphRAG, context, agents)
licence_pricing: Pricing page publishes Aura tiers and a free start; exact AuraDB rates and self-managed Enterprise terms not captured (unknown). Self-managed Enterprise is quote-based
deployment: AuraDB fully managed; self-managed server; Virtual Graph; Aura Graph Analytics; Aura Agent
inputs: CSV/import, Cypher, drivers; GraphRAG adds LLM providers, embeddings and vector index; Neo4j >=5.18.1, Aura >=5.18.0, 2026.01+ for SEARCH filtering; Python 3.10-3.14
entry_criteria: Cypher and property-graph modelling skill; for GraphRAG an LLM key and embedding model
how_layer_built: Two paths: hand-modelled property graph (labels, relationship types, constraints, Cypher) or LLM-assisted Knowledge Graph Builder that extracts entities/relations from documents with resolvers (SpaCy semantic match, fuzzy match) and vector index
automation_level: High for document-to-graph extraction; low for relational/CSV-to-graph (still human modelling)
human_in_loop: GraphRAG pipelines configurable and resolvers can be tuned; no approval UI documented; hand-modelled graphs are human-owned
artifacts_exit_criteria: Graph database, vector index, retrieval pipelines, Context Engine/Aura Agent context
time_versioning: ACID transactions; no documented valid-from/valid-to edge model; temporal queries are a customer design problem (D)
lineage_provenance: GraphRAG returns retrieved chunks/subgraph; no documented per-edge provenance; vector search is approximate (ANN)
agent_consumption: Strongest in set: GraphRAG retrievers, Context Engine, Aura Agent, MCP integration, agent-memory labs
problems_solved: Fraud/AML rings, recommendations, master data/identity, supply chain, network/IT, GraphRAG accuracy, agent memory
documented_outcomes: Vendor-commissioned IDC business-value study and customer stories (e.g. Transport for London); vendor-reported, not measured
limits: Property graph is not a formal ontology; schema optional so graphs drift; extraction quality drives GraphRAG quality; ANN approximate; cluster cost; no time-valid edges or fact provenance
gap_for_us: Sells engine plus modelling labour; we can sell the derived graph (instances, links, time, provenance) and export to Neo4j when traversal/ecosystem is wanted
notes: Pricing page https://neo4j.com/pricing/ exists but body truncated; do not quote Aura rates. Product surface taken from Neo4j navigation.

category: Managed in-memory graph analytics engine; GraphRAG backend for Bedrock
licence_pricing: AWS-managed, per m-NCU-hour plus storage; exact list rates not captured (unknown)
deployment: AWS managed; GraphRAG in 7 regions (Frankfurt, London, Ireland, Oregon, N. Virginia, Tokyo, Singapore)
inputs: Load from S3 or Neptune Database snapshot; Bedrock GraphRAG data source S3 only, up to 1,000 files per data source (raisable to 10,000 by request)
entry_criteria: AWS account and IAM; graph created; for GraphRAG a Knowledge Base, S3 data and a foundation model for graph construction
how_layer_built: Algorithms library and low-latency queries with vector search in traversals; GraphRAG: fully managed LLM graph construction (no customization of graph build), then vector search plus graph expansion at retrieval
automation_level: High for construction in GraphRAG but not tunable; configuration options to customize graph build are not supported
human_in_loop: None documented for GraphRAG build; only model selection
artifacts_exit_criteria: Neptune Analytics graph, vector index, Knowledge Base retrieval, grounded answers
lineage_provenance: Retrieval returns used chunks/nodes; no per-edge evidence or confidence; deleting KB does not delete graph and charges continue
agent_consumption: Bedrock Knowledge Bases plus foundation models (Bedrock Agents)
problems_solved: Cross-document reasoning, GraphRAG over document corpora, fraud/identity analytics, graph algorithms at scale
documented_outcomes: AWS blog/customer references; vendor marketing, not independently verified
limits: S3-only, 1,000-file default, no graph-build customization, no autoscaling for Neptune Analytics graphs, region limits, deletion/cost trap
gap_for_us: AWS gives a black-box document graph; our opening is deterministic inspectable graph construction from structured sources with explainable entity types and per-edge provenance
notes: Engine description from https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune-analytics/latest/userguide/what-is-neptune-analytics.html. RDF support not verified in fetched pages.

category: Virtual instance graph over RDBMS/NoSQL without copying data
licence_pricing: Free tier (no HA/backups/LDAP/full connectors); Enterprise quote-only
inputs: JDBC sources with customer-supplied drivers; SMS/R2RML/SMS2 mappings; materialization via virtual import
how_layer_built: Declarative mappings (or R2RML direct mapping for RDBMS); SPARQL rewritten to SQL and pushed down; virtual transparency merges virtual and local graphs; optional materialization
automation_level: Low: mappings human-authored; direct mapping table-level only
artifacts_exit_criteria: Registered virtual graphs, materialized copies, SPARQL/GraphQL/SQL/BI access, reasoning explanations
time_versioning: Point-in-time recovery; named graphs (D); no bitemporal edges
lineage_provenance: Inference explanation/debugging; inference provenance, not source provenance
problems_solved: Data fabric without ETL, analytics modernization, operational risk, supply chain
documented_outcomes: Vendor customer stories; not independently verified
limits: Documented SPARQL-to-SQL gaps; pushdown-dependent performance; skills scarcity; connector breadth paywalled
gap_for_us: No-copy idea is right but delivery needs specialists; we can do no-copy for files/small DBs with an auto-derived model and no SPARQL
notes: Cross-listed from Layer 1; Layer 2 angle is the virtual instance graph.

category: Distributed MPP graph database with GSQL and GraphStudio
licence_pricing: Savanna free trial $0 per GB/month for 24x7 service, US/Tier 1; paid Savanna and self-managed DB contact sales (quote-only); Community Edition free single server
deployment: Savanna SaaS; self-managed Linux; Community in Docker/single server
inputs: Schema-defined vertices and edges; loading jobs; Kafka/stream connectors
entry_criteria: Must design schema (vertices/edges/types), write a loading job and install GSQL queries
how_layer_built: Code-first manual: GSQL schema + loading + compiled queries exposed as REST endpoints; GraphStudio for visual exploration; no auto-inference from sources
human_in_loop: Developers own schema and queries; changes are code changes
artifacts_exit_criteria: Loaded graph, installed queries callable via REST, GraphStudio visuals
agent_consumption: Vendor markets GraphRAG, vector and agentic AI; specifics not verified
problems_solved: Fraud/AML, customer 360, entity resolution, recommendations, supply chain, cybersecurity, deep-link analytics
documented_outcomes: Named customer pages (Ford, Intuit, Jaguar Land Rover, Microsoft Xbox); vendor marketing
limits: Schema-first, GSQL learning curve, heavy operational footprint, enterprise pricing; wrong tool for small data
gap_for_us: Their buyers buy throughput, not semantics; our story is no schema authoring, no new query language, instant graph for small/medium data
notes: Editions from https://www.tigergraph.com/comparison-of-tigergraph-editions/. Paid list prices not captured (contact sales).

category: In-memory graph database, Cypher-compatible, real-time and AI memory
licence_pricing: Community Edition free forever and open source; Enterprise and AI Platform priced by memory capacity (quote-only); 30-day enterprise trial; Cloud 1-32 GB RAM; OEM/SaaS licence available
deployment: Self-managed; Memgraph Cloud (AWS, 6 regions); AWS Marketplace; OEM embedded
inputs: Cypher, stream connectors (Kafka, Pulsar, Redpanda), vector search, MAGE algorithms; ZeroETL marketed
entry_criteria: Cypher skill plus memory sizing; ops for in-memory deployment
how_layer_built: Hand-modelled property graph plus Cypher; streams for updates; vector index for similarity; MAGE algorithms
automation_level: Low: no documented auto-modelling from relational sources
human_in_loop: Developers own model, queries and memory sizing
artifacts_exit_criteria: In-memory graph, algorithms, vector search, REST/Bolt access
agent_consumption: GraphRAG and AI-memory positioning; exact integrations not verified
problems_solved: Real-time fraud/risk, 360-degree network exploration, logistics/network optimization, GraphRAG/AI memory
documented_outcomes: Vendor customer stories; not independently verified
limits: Memory-bound cost, in-memory ops care, no semantic/ontology layer, no documented temporal model
gap_for_us: Engine waiting for a modeller; our auto-derived time-aware graph is a different product rather than a worse engine
notes: Community Edition described as production-ready open source on the pricing page.

category: Spark graph-analytics library, not a graph store
inputs: Vertex DataFrame (id) and edge DataFrame (src, dst); optional properties
how_layer_built: Code-first: GraphFrame(vertices, edges) then algorithms (PageRank, connected components, motif finding, Pregel, aggregate messages, label propagation, shortest paths); the graph is the DataFrame pair
automation_level: None for modelling; algorithms are automated
artifacts_exit_criteria: Algorithm output DataFrames (component ids, ranks, motifs); not a queryable graph for apps or agents
problems_solved: Entity resolution at scale via connected components, fraud cycle detection, compliance shortest paths, social/marketing analytics, graph ML and embeddings
documented_outcomes: Databricks engineering blogs; no measured independent outcome data
limits: Batch analytics; no persistence or traversal API for apps; no ontology; no lineage; maintained by individual contributors, no vendor SLA
gap_for_us: Proves demand for graph algorithms on existing tables but leaves the graph unbuilt; we produce the graph and time bounds, algorithms are a thin add-on
notes: API metadata is measured (A). README at https://github.com/graphframes/graphframes documents capabilities (B).

category: Cloud data warehouse; hierarchies via recursive SQL, no native graph engine
licence_pricing: Warehouse credits; no graph-specific SKU; recursive queries consume warehouse time like any SQL (D)
entry_criteria: SQL skill; hierarchy already modelled relationally
how_layer_built: Hand-written SQL: anchor clause plus recursive clause with UNION ALL; Snowflake documents the working-table iteration model and restrictions
human_in_loop: SQL author is the whole loop
artifacts_exit_criteria: Result sets only; no reusable graph object, model or API
time_versioning: Table-level Time Travel exists (not verified this pass); no graph-level as-of semantics
lineage_provenance: Not applicable at graph level; warehouse lineage is a separate feature (see Layer 1)
agent_consumption: SQL only; Snowflake AI features not assessed
problems_solved: Org-chart/BOM rollups, simple multi-hop chains, who-reports-to-whom
limits: Recursive clause cannot use aggregate/window functions, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT or DISTINCT; wrong construction loops until statement timeout; no graph algorithms, centrality, shortest path or identity resolution
gap_for_us: Largest addressable segment: teams already doing graph in SQL who would try a derived graph with as-of queries if it cost nothing
notes: Some brief claims (e.g. no native graph type) rest on absence in the query docs reviewed; flagged D where inferred.

category: Embedded property graph database, Cypher, MIT
licence_pricing: Free, MIT licence; repo archived so no commercial support or upstream patches
inputs: Cypher graph loaded from files/dataframes; vector and full-text search built in
how_layer_built: Embedded Cypher graph; no server or managed service; algorithms via Cypher
problems_solved: Prototypes and embedded graph use cases (pre-archive)
limits: Archived 2025-10-10 (last push); 329 open issues; kuzudb.com DNS failure at access; acquisition reported in market but not verified from primary source
gap_for_us: Lesson: free embedded graph is not a durable platform; we must own data in boring portable formats, keep export paths and a model/provenance record that survives an engine swap
notes: Measured via GitHub API: archived=true, pushed_at=2025-10-10, MIT, 4018 stars. Acquisition NOT verified; do not state it as fact.
